properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 8:41AM PDT until October 16 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY NEW FIRE STARTS
THURSDAY THROUGH SATURDAY DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY STRONG SANTA
ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.No changes from previous statement. Moderate to locally strong
Santa Ana winds will quickly develop on Thursday, peak Thursday
afternoon through Friday afternoon, then slowly weaken through the
weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will settle over the region and dry
out any effects of the recent rains. Red Flag Warnings are in
effect for most of Los Angeles and Ventura Counties Thursday
through Saturday, and for interior Santa Barbara and San Luis
Obispo Counties for Friday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Cuyama Valley, San Luis Obispo County
Mountains and Santa Barbara County Interior Mountains.

* TIMING...From 3 AM to 6 PM PDT Friday.

* WINDS...East 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 15 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM LATE TONIGHT THROUGH
FRIDAY AFTERNOON...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 418 including Lake
Pillsbury, 419 including the City of Clearlake, Middletown,
Lower Lake, Indian Valley Reservoir, and other areas in
eastern and southern Lake County.

* WIND...Sustained winds of 15-20mph with gusts to 30 mph possible
in exposed areas .

* HUMIDITY...Low overnight recoveries of 30-35% will drop to 10-
20% through the morning. Very poor RH recovery into Friday.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 15 at 1:38AM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Elevated high tides 6.5 to 7 ft will return late this
morning, along with surf of 3 to 5 ft with sets to 6 ft.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding and beach erosion. Dangerous
swimming conditions for inexperienced swimmers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will fall below 6.5 ft after
today's high tide. A long-period south swell will continue
today.
properties.instruction:
A beach hazards statement for minor tidal overflow means that
high astronomical tides possibly in combination with above normal
surf will likely produce minor flooding of low-lying areas along
the beach such as beach parking lots. Coastal officials should
take the necessary precautionary measures to safeguard their
beaches.

A beach hazards statement is issued when threats such as rip
currents and other hazards are possible. Caution should be used
when in or near the water.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 15 at 12:23AM MST until October 16 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...In Arizona, Parker Valley. In California, Chuckwalla
Mountains, Chuckwalla Valley, Imperial County Southeast, and Palo
Verde Valley.

* WHEN...From 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ this evening to 2 PM MST /2 PM PDT/
Friday.

* IMPACTS...Difficult driving conditions, especially for larger
vehicles traveling along roads with crosswinds. Light, unsecured
objects may become airborne.
properties.instruction:
A Wind Advisory means that sustained wind speeds of between 30 and 40
mph are expected, or wind gusts of between 40 and 58 mph. Winds this
strong can make driving difficult, especially for high profile
vehicles.

In addition, strong winds over desert areas could result in briefly
lowered visibilities to well under a mile at times in blowing dust or
blowing sand. Use extra caution.

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Mountains
properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 15 at 12:18AM PDT until October 16 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM THIS EVENING THROUGH FRIDAY
MORNING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTH BAY INTERIOR
MOUNTAINS...

.Moderate offshore winds are expected to develop Thursday night into
Friday morning over the North Bay Interior Mountains. Conditions will
be very dry with very poor overnight humidity recoveries only
reaching 14 to 24 percent. Rapid fire spread is possible given the
combination of gusty northerly winds and very dry overnight
conditions.

The National Weather Service in San Francisco CA has issued a Fire
Weather Watch.

* AFFECTED AREA...North Bay Interior Mountains.

* TIMING...From this evening through Friday morning.

* WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 14 to 24 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are
forecast during the valid watch time. These conditions could promote
the rapid spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening.
Check weather.gov/mtr for forecast updates and a possible upgrade of
this watch to a Red Flag Warning. Also consider signing up for your
city, county, or state emergency alert system.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

properties.headline: Lake Wind Advisory issued October 14 at 11:22PM PDT until October 16 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph and waves 2
to 3 feet for Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 7 PM Thursday to 2 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds and rough waves on area lakes will create
hazardous conditions for small craft.
properties.instruction:
Check lake conditions before heading out and be prepared for a sudden
increase in winds and wave heights. Consider postponing boating
activities on the lake until a day with less wind.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 14 at 12:27PM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor tidal overflow during times of high tides,
dangerous rip currents, and elevated surf.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding of sea water is likely around high
tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with
normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is possible. The
risk for significant damage is very low. There is an increased
risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and
surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal overflow during morning high
tide of 6.4 feet.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
